text:
amanda: Hey team — customer hitting timeouts when doing very long generations (8-12k tokens). They pass timeout=600 to the Python client but stream cuts after ~60s. Repro attached.

amanda: Minimal repro they gave:
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=..., timeout=600)
resp = c.generate(model='gpt-xl', prompt='...' , stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text)
```
They say partial output, then SDK raises TimeoutError after ~60s.

carla_support: thanks — can you paste the exact SDK version and whether they set any env vars? also any proxy in front (ALB/ingress)?

amanda: SDK reported 0.3.1. No explicit proxy, but they're on corporate NAT + outbound proxy. No custom env vars set (I think).

mike_eng: 0.3.1 rings a bell — we changed streaming default read timeout behavior in 0.3.4. Older clients used httpx default which had 60s read chunk timeout. If they passed timeout=600 it was applied to total request but not to per-chunk streaming read in that old branch.

amanda: interesting. so timeout arg meant "total" but chunk/read had separate default in older SDKs?

mike_eng: yeah. TL;DR: before fix, we layered timeouts: connect || total || per-read. The public param mapped to total, but httpx still enforced a per-read deadline of 60s. With long token gaps (model slow), you hit read cutoff.

ryan_dev: quick workaround: upgrade to >=0.3.4 which unifies streaming/read timeouts or explicitly configure httpx Timeout with read set to a larger value. Example we gave customers:
```
from httpx import Timeout
c = Client(..., httpx_timeout=Timeout(connect=10.0, read=600.0))
```
That bypasses the old per-chunk default.

amanda: customer tried upgrade to 0.3.4 and says streaming no longer cuts off. they asked why docs don't mention the env var name for legacy behavior — I couldn't find REDWOOD_TIMEOUT env details.

mike_eng: docs gap — agreed. There's also confusion with REDWOOD_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS vs REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS in historical deployments. Old installers set the ms var, new SDK prefers seconds and named REDWOOD_TIMEOUT. I'll file a docs task.

carla_support: can we add quick reproduction/triage steps here for support handbook? I want a checklist: check sdk version, check proxy/ALB idle timeout, ask for httpx config, ask for sample stream output and last chunk timestamp.

mike_eng: suggested checklist (short):
- ask SDK version
- check for corporate proxy/ALB and its idle timeout
- ask whether they used timeout arg vs env var
- ask for sample logs showing last successful chunk and error
- suggest temporary upgrade to 0.3.4 or set httpx_timeout read param

amanda: noting also that retries can mask this: if client retries whole request after a read cutoff, upstream may have produced partial tokens and that can look like duplicate output. Customer saw repeated prefixes when retries triggered mid-stream.

ryan_dev: yep — streaming + automatic retry = tricky. We recommend disabling automatic retries for streaming requests or using idempotency keys at the app layer. I'll add a small blurb in the KB.

sre-bot: incident-note: flagged potential product bug: per-chunk read timeout not honoring client.total in SDK <=0.3.3. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

carla_support: resolved for this customer: upgrade to 0.3.4 fixed it. Filed docs PR about env var names and support checklist. Closing after follow-up in 24h.

amanda: thanks all :heart:
